messages:
Priya: Hey team — need a quick alignment on the Q2 prefetch/prefill pilot: product is asking for steady 2k rps p95 ~250ms with the ability to absorb 5k rps bursts for ~15m. We also need a safe, documented fallback when capacity is tight. Can eng/runtime/infra/security confirm constraints? cc @Ethan @Maya @Leo @Sam
Ethan: Confirming numbers. Main questions: do we want dedicated prewarm slots or rely on autoscale + aggressive prefill? Prefill sounds safer for p95.
Maya: Runtime preference is dedicated prewarm + prefix/KV prefill for top ~75 prefixes. Propose 10 minute prewarm window and a prefix whitelist that we can iterate on. Need a clear fallback model id (smaller quantized variant) and a route flag to trigger it.
Leo: Infra can carve out reserved burst nodes but requires 48h notice to scheduler. I can start the reservation today if we commit to exact node counts. Also: if we need KMS-managed keys for customer data, open ticket now — rotations will need a midnight maintenance window.
Priya: KMS is required for this pilot. I'll open the ticket this afternoon. Launch SLA we9re aiming for: 99.9% availability first 30 days.
Sam: Security ok on KMS + auditing. Need an abbreviated threat-model review and an IaC policy for least-privilege key access. Also confirm telemetry doesn't ship PII.
Ethan: For rollouts I want tenant-scoped canaries so we can ramp traffic with real workloads. Plan: route flag + rollout policy. Can runtime implement?
Maya: Yes — runtime supports percentage canaries. Example rollout config we'll use: ```json
{"route":"canary","percent":3,"fallback_model":"redwood-micro-q8"}
``` This allows us to validate warmup and fallback behavior on a small subset before full cutover.
Leo: I'll provision 2x burst nodes and set an autoscale window to 20 minutes. Reservation ETA: tomorrow morning; I'll post the reservation ID when created.
Priya: Actions: Priya -> open KMS ticket (#TICKET-4422); Ethan -> add canary flag + document fallback behavior by Tue; Maya -> produce prefix warm list + attach eval prompts; Leo -> reserve burst nodes and post ID; Sam -> schedule threat-model w/in 48h. Any blockers?
Ethan: One ask: document expected quality delta for the fallback model (latency vs embedding/semantic-match metrics) so product can sign off tradeoffs.
Maya: Will attach eval curve and token-cost delta to the spec. Track metrics: gen latency, semantic top-k match, token cost difference, and rollback triggers.
ops-bot: rolling update: canary-flag toggled in staging at 2024-05-08T04:15Z
Priya: Cool. If no objections by EOD I9ll lock scope and instruct PMs to start customer comms.
